blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. On the 200 ReXGroundingCT validation scans, CTLink achieved a hit rate of 0.816, an instance F1 score of 0.456, and a mean Dice score of 0.400, compared with 0.533, 0.175, and 0.234 for VoxTell, a publicly available text-prompted segmentation model (P < .001 for all). On the test set of the MICCAI 2026 ReXGrounding challenge, an ensemble of seven CTLink models achieved the highest hit rate (0.782) and instance F1 score (0.386) of all 48 participating teams. On 50 test scans segmented twice by independent radiologists, CTLink matched or exceeded inter-rater agreement. Diffuse non-focal findings remained the main limitation, partly because their extent is outlined inconsistently even between radiologists. The CTLink model weights are available at https://huggingface.co/rajpurkarlab/CTLink, and the dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGroundingCT.

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Radiologists record the findings of an imaging examination in a radiology report, which describes each finding in
text only, without marking it on the scan. Referring clinicians who want to see a described finding must therefore locate it on the scan themselves, which takes time and can be ambiguous when a scan contains several similar abnormalities.
When findings are visually marked on the scan, referring clinicians plan management faster and more confidently ( 1 ) .
A model that segments the finding described by each report sentence would automatically highlight that finding on the scan,
linking every sentence to the abnormality it describes. Such a model would spare referring clinicians the
search for each described finding, make it easier to compare findings with those on prior examinations, and make
AI-generated reports more verifiable ( 2 , 3 , 4 ) .

blocks.en:
For three-dimensional scans such as chest CT, the task of segmenting the findings described by report sentences remains difficult ( 5 ) . A report sentence
specifies a finding by its appearance, size, and location, often among several similar abnormalities in the same
scan. Most segmentation models, however, are trained to segment a fixed set of organs or lesion types ( 6 , 7 ) , accepting only a category name, such as “nodule” or
“tumor,” as the prompt ( 8 , 9 , 10 , 11 ) . Such models perform poorly on free-text report sentences ( 5 ) , because these sentences differ from the short category names
the models were trained on. Linking phrases to the image regions they describe, a task known as visual grounding ( 12 , 13 ) , has been studied in radiology mainly on chest radiographs, with bounding boxes rather than segmentations ( 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 , 3 ) . More recent work on CT has linked report text to anatomical regions, such as organs or lung lobes ( 18 , 19 ) , or has localized findings with bounding boxes ( 20 ) , rather than segmenting the described findings. Progress has long been limited by the lack of a public dataset that pairs report sentences with segmentations of the described findings. ReXGroundingCT now provides such data, linking findings from chest CT reports ( 21 ) to 3D segmentation masks ( 4 ) . Models trained with ReXGroundingCT, such as VoxTell ( 22 ) and DAGG ( 23 ) ,
have substantially advanced performance on this task but have not reached the level of agreement between radiologists ( 4 ) .

blocks.en:
We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted segmentation model for linking radiology report findings to 3D chest CT scans. To train it, we create ReXGroundingCTv2, which adds 1134 chest CT scans with every instance of each finding segmented to ReXGroundingCT.
On the ReXGroundingCT validation set, CTLink localizes 82% of findings, compared with 53% for VoxTell. On 50 test scans segmented twice by independent radiologists ( 4 ) , CTLink matches or exceeds inter-rater agreement.
On the test set of the ReXGrounding challenge at MICCAI 2026, an ensemble of CTLink
models localizes more findings (78%) and achieves a higher instance F1 score (0.39) than the entries of all 48
participating teams ( 24 ) .
We publicly release the CTLink model weights and ReXGroundingCTv2 to further support research in this direction.

blocks.en:
This retrospective study used de-identified noncontrast chest CT scans and radiology reports from CT-RATE ( 21 ) , a public dataset acquired during routine care at Istanbul Medipol University Mega
Hospital, Turkey, and released under its own ethics approval.
Additional institutional review board approval was not required.

7687 findings, with at most three instances annotated per finding ( 4 ) . We used the

training scans with 1895 findings (v2 training set). The 200 ReXGrounding
challenge validation scans (381 findings) were used for the ablation, and the 300 ReXGrounding challenge test scans (582
findings) were used for the comparison with the challenge entries. Eight validation scans and 15 test scans came from patients who also had a
different examination among the scans used for training.

blocks.en: Model
blocks.zh: 型号

blocks.en:
CTLink used the same architecture as VoxTell v1.1 ( 22 ) : a residual-encoder 3D U-Net ( 6 ) image
encoder and a transformer prompt decoder. In the prompt decoder, the sentence embedding, computed by a frozen Qwen3-Embedding-4B
model ( 25 ) , attended to the image features, and the resulting text features were fused with the decoder features at every stage. Each finding sentence was one
prompt, and the output was a binary mask in the native CT voxel grid. Figure 1 shows the architecture.

blocks.zh: 培训

blocks.en:
All models were fine-tuned from the VoxTell v1.1 weights. This version was trained on 190 public datasets and drew only 5% of its training samples from instance-focused datasets such as ReXGroundingCT ( 22 ) , so report sentences were a small part of its training. Each training sample was one scan–finding pair,
with a random 3D crop of 192 3 192^{3} voxels that was centered on the finding in 50% of samples. Training used
a combined Dice and binary cross-entropy loss with deep supervision and the AdamW optimizer (learning rate 1 × 10 − 5 1\times 10^{-5} , 500-iteration
linear warm-up, cosine decay) for 50 000 iterations with a batch size of two (100 000 training samples). For v1 findings with three annotated
instances, background voxels were down-weighted (weight, 0.3), because further instances may be unlabeled.

blocks.en: Post-processing
blocks.zh: 后处理

blocks.en:
We applied four post-processing steps. First, predictions were restricted to the lobes named in the sentence, using the lung lobe masks provided with CT-RATE (generated with
TotalSegmentator ( 7 ) ) dilated by 32 voxels. Second, non-focal findings other than emphysema used a probability threshold of 0.9 instead of
0.5, because the model over-segmented these diffuse findings relative to the reference masks. Third, emphysema
predictions were kept only in lung with attenuation below − 910 -910 HU, plus a three-voxel margin, because emphysema appears
on CT as lung with abnormally low attenuation ( 26 ) . Finally, connected components smaller than 5% of the largest component of the finding were
removed. Post-processing settings were selected on the validation set and the public half of the ReXGrounding challenge
test set (150 scans).

blocks.en: CTLink Ensemble
blocks.zh: CTLink 组合

blocks.en:
We also trained an ensemble of seven CTLink models as our entry for the ReXGrounding challenge comparison
(Table 3 ). The ensemble averaged the probability maps of its members, which were selected on the public half of the ReXGrounding challenge test set (150 scans), as was possible for teams
during the challenge’s public leaderboard phase. The members were five trainings of the CTLink recipe with different random seeds and two variants, one trained with non-focal findings sampled three times as often and one fine-tuned for 10 000 iterations without the non-focal findings of v1 scans. Post-processing was the same as for CTLink, except that, because averaging lowers the probabilities of the members, the mean probability map was thresholded at 0.35 instead of 0.5 (0.8 instead of 0.9 for non-focal findings other than emphysema), and predicted components smaller than 50 voxels were removed.

blocks.en: Robustness Analysis
blocks.zh: 强性分析

blocks.en:
To test the robustness of CTLink to phrasing, we evaluated it on edited versions of the 582 test finding sentences. A large
language model (GPT-6.1-sol; OpenAI) edited each sentence in five ways: (1) replacing terms, such as finding names or
locations, with synonyms that radiologists typically use in chest CT reports, (2) replacing terms with standard radiology abbreviations, (3) freely rewording the whole
sentence, (4) for findings in both lungs, splitting the sentence into a left-lung and a right-lung sentence, and (5) for
findings in two or more lobes of one lung, splitting the sentence into one sentence per lobe. Details of the process are given in Appendix Appendix S2: Instance F1 Score of the Second Segmentation .

blocks.en: Error Analysis
blocks.zh: 错误分析

blocks.en:
Each finding in the ReXGrounding challenge test set that the CTLink ensemble missed (Dice score < < 0.1) was assigned automatically to one of four error types:
an empty prediction, partial overlap with the reference (Dice score above 0 but below 0.1), a prediction in the lobe of
the reference without overlap (a different lesion in the right place), or a prediction outside that lobe (wrong
location).

空预测,与参考文献部分重叠(比分高于0,但低于0.1),在叶中预测

For the 31 findings in two or more lobes of one lung, requesting each lobe separately gave a hit rate of 0.806, compared with 0.710 for the
original sentence ( P = .07 P=.07 ), and without post-processing, 78% of the voxels predicted for a single lobe lay in the requested lobe.

blocks.en: Error Analysis
blocks.zh: 错误分析

blocks.en:
Of the 127 test findings that the CTLink ensemble missed (examples in Figure 6 ), 3 (2%) had an empty prediction, 75 (59%) overlapped the
reference partially, 22 (17%) had a prediction in the lobe of the reference without overlap, and 27 (21%) had a
prediction in another location. Partial overlap was the most common error type for both focal (58 of 97, 60%) and
non-focal findings (17 of 30, 57%). Some misses reflected the reference masks or a related abnormality rather than a failure to localize (Figure 6 ). For “Multiple pulmonary nodules in both lungs,” the reference masks extended beyond the nodules that the CTLink ensemble segmented. For “Small fluid loculations in the fissures,” it segmented the pleural fluid at the lung bases, and for “Emphysematous air densities in right anterior chest wall,” it segmented the pneumothorax along the right lung instead of the air in the chest wall.

blocks.zh: 讨论情况

blocks.en:
We developed CTLink, a text-prompted segmentation model for linking radiology report findings to 3D chest CT scans. To train it, we created ReXGroundingCTv2, which adds 1134 exhaustively annotated scans to ReXGroundingCT. CTLink localized 82% of findings on
the ReXGroundingCT validation set, matched or exceeded radiologist inter-rater agreement on 50 test scans, and an ensemble of CTLink models had the highest hit rate and instance F1 score of all entries of the ReXGrounding
challenge. At this level, CTLink could mark most reported findings on the scan for referring clinicians,
and even most of the findings that the CTLink ensemble missed (75 of 127) overlapped the reference partially. The ablation showed that training data drove most of these gains: fine-tuning VoxTell on the
v1 training set, which had been only a small part of its pretraining, gave by far the largest improvement, and adding
the exhaustively annotated v2 training set the largest further gain in Dice score.

我们开发了CTLink,一种文本催化分解模型,将放射学报告结果与3D胸腔CT扫描联系起来. 为了训练它,我们创建了ReXGroundingCTv2,在ReXGroundingCT中增加了1134个详尽注解的扫描. CTLink 本地化 82%的调查结果

挑战。 在这一层面,CTLink可以在扫描中标出大多数报告的调查结果,以便推荐临床医生,
甚至是大部分CTLink综艺节目错过(127个节目中的75个)的发现,都部分重复了参考内容. 减幅表明,培训数据驱动了大多数这些成果:

blocks.en:
Our study had several limitations. First, non-focal findings, such as emphysema and bronchiectasis, remained the hardest part
of the task, partly because the extent of a diffuse finding is hard to outline consistently. In the inter-rater study
of ReXGroundingCT, the second radiologist segmentation reached a hit rate of only 0.41 for non-focal findings against the
reference masks, compared with 0.84 for focal findings ( 4 ) , and reader agreement on diffuse lung disease at CT is moderate
even for visual assessment ( 27 , 28 ) . Second, all scans came from CT-RATE, a single-center collection of
noncontrast chest CT scans, so performance on contrast-enhanced scans, other scanners, and other populations is
unknown. Third, each reference mask was drawn by one annotator, although readers disagree even on which lung nodules
are present ( 29 ) . Fourth, the comparison
with radiologists covered only 50 scans (96 findings). Finally, CTLink covers only findings of the lungs, airways, and pleura.

blocks.en:
In conclusion, CTLink localized the findings described in chest CT reports at the level of agreement between
radiologists, showing that report sentences can be linked automatically to the abnormalities they describe. Such
links could let referring clinicians see each reported finding on the scan, make it easier to compare findings with
prior examinations, and let readers verify AI-generated reports. Our results also showed that
exhaustive and accurate annotation of the training data mattered more than changes to the training procedure, which
should guide the design of future datasets.
Future work should
extend the approach to other body regions and imaging modalities, and establish consistent
annotation of diffuse findings. We release CTLink and ReXGroundingCTv2 to support this work.

Table 4 gives an instance F1 score of 0.417 for the second segmentation, whereas the inter-rater

challenge evaluator, which we used for every model and for the second segmentation, instead counts each connected
component of a mask as one instance, so a lesion drawn with disconnected parts counts as several instances. Scoring all masks with the evaluator keeps CTLink and the radiologists comparable. Hit

blocks.en:
The rewritten sentences were generated with GPT-6.1-sol (version 2026-09-29; OpenAI) and checked with GPT-6-astra (version 2026-09-03; OpenAI), with the prompts in Figures S1 to S3 . For each of the 582 test findings, the model wrote (1) a version in which terms were replaced only with synonyms that radiologists commonly write in their place with exactly the same meaning (for example, “Dependent atelectasis in both lower lobe basal segments” became “Dependent atelectasis in bilateral lower lobe basal segments”), (2) a version with standard radiology abbreviations (such as RUL, GGO, and bilat.), and (3) a version freely reworded as another radiologist would write it. (4) It also judged whether the finding involved both lungs (307
findings) and, if so, wrote a left-lung and a right-lung sentence that kept the finding type, the descriptors that apply
to every lesion, and the locations on that side (for example, “Scarring in the apical segments of the upper lobes of both lungs” became “Scarring in
the apical segment of the left upper lobe” and “Scarring in the apical segment of the right upper lobe”). (5) In the same way, it decided which lobes the finding involved, as stated or clearly implied by the sentence, and, for a finding in two or more lobes, wrote one sentence per lobe (34 findings involved two or more lobes of one lung).

Hit recall is the proportion of findings with a Dice score of at least 0.1 (the hit rate), and hit precision is the proportion of findings with a nonempty prediction that were hits.
blocks.zh: 表S2:CTLink的精度和回溯以及测试集上的挑战条目. 数据是ReXGrounding挑战测试集的值. 实例精确度和召回度将预测中相连的元件与附加说明的参考例相匹配(在Dice分数 \\ geq 0.2 中匹配;预言中小于10 voxels的元件被忽略). 命中召回(英語:Hit recall)是至少得分0.1分(命中率)的发现比例,命中精确度是命中时非空预测的发现比例.

blocks.en: Table S4: Robustness Analysis: Effect of Phrasing. Data are for the ReXGrounding challenge test set. Each edit is compared with the original ReXGroundingCT sentence on the findings whose sentence the edit changed. The left-right split covers the 290 findings in both lungs, with the left-lung and right-lung predictions combined. The lobe split covers the 31 findings in two or more lobes of one lung, with the per-lobe predictions combined. Agreement is the median Dice score between the masks predicted for the original and the edited sentence. Mean Dice score per scan.
blocks.zh: 表S4:强力分析:误差效应. 数据用于ReXGrounding挑战测试集. 每一个编辑都与编辑更改的句子上的结论的原始REXG回合CT句比较. 左-右分裂覆盖了两肺的290个发现,左倾和右倾的预测结合. 叶片分裂覆盖一个肺的两个或两个以上叶片的31个发现,每个叶片的预测结合. 协议(Agreement)是原声和编辑后的句子所预言的口罩之间的二分分中位数. 平均值 每次扫描都得分
